metaDescription: Six pressure washers at or under $100, from corded Greenworks and Sun Joe units to cordless handhelds, compared on PSI, GPM and what they can actually clean.
expertTake: The Greenworks 1700 PSI at 1.2 GPM is the best overall pick, because its flow figure is stated and it is built for the light residential jobs this price band can really do. The Westinghouse ePX3100s is the value pick for the biggest max PSI and a foam cannon. Anyone with a driveway, deck or siding to strip should skip this band.
introParagraphs: At the lowest price, a pressure washer is a light-duty tool for cars, bikes, patio furniture and grills. It cannot strip paint or etch a driveway, and expecting that is the quickest way to feel cheated.

The honest comparison is between corded electrics with a stated flow rate and cordless handhelds that run off a battery. Prices move, and the $100 cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: Greenworks 1700 PSI 1.2 GPM Electric Pressure Washer
products.description:
Cleaning power comes from pressure and flow together, and the Greenworks lists both: 1700 PSI at 1.2 GPM. Multiplying them gives about 2,040 cleaning units, a useful way to compare machines that quote different PSI headlines. The listing positions it for light residential cleaning of cars, trucks, patio furniture and similar jobs, which is the honest scope of a washer in this class.

Compared with the Westinghouse ePX3100s, which advertises 2100 max PSI, the Greenworks is more modest, but its flow is stated plainly, while the Westinghouse figure of 1.76 GPM is a maximum reached at the lowest pressure setting. Electric washers quote a max PSI that is a peak rather than a sustained number, so a plain 1700 and 1.2 reads as the more believable pair.

Ownership is simple: no gas, no oil, no spark plugs, no air filter and no pull cord. Drain the pump and hose before freezing weather and avoid running it dry. It is the pick for a household that washes cars and furniture a few times a year. Always test a new spray pattern on a hidden spot first, and keep the tip at least a foot from painted surfaces. Wear closed shoes, because water at this pressure can still bruise a foot. Keep a small bucket of clean water nearby to prime the pump if the flow sputters at startup.
products.bestFor: Cars, patio furniture and light residential cleanup.
pros: Stated flow of 1.2 GPM alongside pressure
No gas, oil or spark plug upkeep
cons: Too light for driveways and decks

products.name: Westinghouse ePX3100s 2100 Max PSI Electric Pressure Washer
products.description:
The ePX3100s advertises the largest max PSI in the group at 2100 and ships with a foam cannon and a turbo nozzle. A turbo nozzle spins a 0 degree jet in a cone, which cleans faster than a fixed fan tip but at the expense of reach and control. The foam cannon is the more useful accessory for car washing.

The flow figure of 1.76 GPM is a maximum reached at the lowest pressure setting, so pressure and flow do not peak at the same time. In other words, the machine does not deliver 2100 PSI at 1.76 GPM. Treat it as a light-duty tool with a bigger peak than the Greenworks, not as a step into driveway cleaning.

Store it drained and indoors during cold weather. It is the value pick for a buyer who wants accessories and a higher peak figure. A foam cannon needs a thin soap mix and a wide tip to produce thick foam, so follow the label on the bottle. Rinse from the top down and let the soap sit for a minute before rinsing.
products.bestFor: Car washing with a foam cannon and turbo tip.
pros: Highest max PSI claim in the group
Foam cannon and turbo nozzle included
Corded power with no battery to age
cons: Peak PSI and peak GPM do not occur together
Max PSI is not sustained pressure

products.name: Sun Joe SPX100-GO 1800 PSI Max Electric Pressure Washer
products.description:
Sun Joe is among the best-known consumer pressure washer brands, and the SPX100-GO is its compact, portable entry. It lists 1800 PSI max, an electric peak figure rather than a sustained rating, and positions itself for all-purpose light cleaning.

The listing gives fewer flow details than the Greenworks, so you cannot calculate cleaning units from it. That is a weakness for comparison, though the brand record on parts and manuals is reassuring.

Keep the inlet screen clean and store it drained. It suits a buyer who values a recognizable name. Because the listing gives little about the pump, expect a basic axial cam design, which is typical for electric consumer machines and not meant to be rebuilt. Use a clean water source and filter if needed.
cons: Flow rate not stated in the listing

products.name: Greenworks 1600 PSI 1.2 GPM Electric Pressure Washer
products.description:
The 1600 PSI model is the lower sibling of the 1700. It keeps the same 1.2 GPM, giving roughly 1,920 cleaning units against about 2,040, a difference you would struggle to notice on a car.

It shares the no-gas, no-oil design of the Greenworks range. If the price is lower than the 1700 on the day, the saving is worth taking.

Drain it before storage. Compared with the 1700 model, the money you save is small, so choose by what the day's listing price allows. Keep the nozzle in a place you will remember, because loose tips go missing.
products.bestFor: Cars and furniture on the tightest budget.

products.name: KEEPEAK Cordless Pressure Washer 1450 PSI 2 x 4.0Ah
products.description:
The KEEPEAK is a handheld that draws water from a bucket or hose and runs on two 4.0Ah batteries. It is not a pressure washer in the sense of a corded unit with a mains-fed pump, because a battery pump cannot sustain the flow of a plug-in machine.

Its 1450 PSI is a peak claim from the pump, and its flow is low, so cleaning units are far lower than a corded Greenworks. Where it wins is portability: you can wash a boat, a bike or a patio chair far from an outlet.

Keep the batteries indoors and rinse the nozzle. Battery washers are limited by the pump, which cannot sustain the flow of a corded machine. Treat the run time as best-case and carry the second battery on longer jobs.
cons: Low flow and peak pressure claims

products.name: OUYESU Cordless Pressure Washer 1200 PSI 30 Pressure Levels
products.description:
The OUYESU offers 30 adjustable pressure levels and a brushless motor, and claims 60 to 90 minutes of run time. Fine control is useful when cleaning delicate surfaces.

The 1200 PSI is the lowest peak in the group, and the run time claim depends on level.

Store it indoors. Fine control is an advantage on thin paint and plastic trim, but remember that low pressure also means slow rinsing. Start at a low level and step up only if needed. Treat the claimed minutes as a best case, and keep the second battery on the charger.
cons: Run time claim is a best case

buyingCriteria.explanation: Cleaning power comes from pressure and flow. Multiplying them gives cleaning units: the Greenworks 1700 at 1.2 GPM is about 2,040, and the 1600 about 1,920. A bigger PSI headline with an unstated or maximum GPM tells you little. Check the length of the cord and hose, since a short hose forces you to move the machine often. Finally, think about where you will use it: a washer that needs a nearby outlet and hose bib is useless at the far end of the yard.

Electric washers quote a max PSI that is a peak. The Westinghouse lists 2100 max PSI and 1.76 max GPM at the lowest pressure, so the two peaks do not occur together. Read both numbers skeptically. Look at whether the unit has an onboard detergent tank or only a bottle, because that changes how you apply soap. Consider buying a small surface cleaner later only if your machine has enough flow to spin it, which none of these do.

Corded units like the Greenworks run on mains power with a real pump, while cordless handhelds such as the KEEPEAK and OUYESU run a small battery pump. Cordless is portable but weak. Match it to the job. A wide stance and a stable base reduce tipping when you pull the hose.

The Westinghouse includes a foam cannon and turbo nozzle, while others offer nozzles only. A foam cannon matters for washing cars, and a turbo nozzle speeds cleaning at the cost of control. Check the inlet filter and keep a spare O-ring, which are small and cheap.

A 0 degree tip can damage surfaces, 15 degree suits hard surfaces and 25 or 40 degree suits general rinsing. Start with a wide tip and move closer. Buy a machine you can lift into the car, since you will move it to the job.

High-pressure water can penetrate skin. Never point it at people or pets, wear eye protection, and avoid running the pump dry. Review the manual for the correct way to start the pump, because trapped air is the main cause of weak flow.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning power
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated PSI and GPM and computed cleaning units where flow was given. The Greenworks 1700 led among stated figures. Stated flow rates earned a lot of credit because they allow a fair comparison.

howWeEvaluated.title: Spec honesty
howWeEvaluated.description: We discounted peak PSI and maximum GPM claims that do not occur together. Plain figures scored higher. Where only peak PSI was listed we marked down for transparency.

howWeEvaluated.title: Accessories
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted foam cannons, nozzles and batteries included. Accessories mattered most for the car washing use case.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered cord reach, battery needs and winter storage. Winter storage and cord length counted toward ownership.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We kept guidance conservative. Owner feedback patterns informed the durability view. Safety guidance stays conservative because even small washers can injure.

cards.label: Corded
cards.text: The Greenworks, Sun Joe and Westinghouse use a mains-fed pump, so they deliver steadier pressure and flow.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: The KEEPEAK and OUYESU go anywhere, but their small pumps limit flow and the battery limits time.

howToChoose.note: Pick corded for a driveway-adjacent car wash; pick cordless for boats and bikes.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Moderate pressure, a wide tip and a foam cannon. Too much pressure can strip paint and clear coat.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Westinghouse ePX3100s with its foam cannon and the OUYESU with 30 levels are the best fits.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a driveway, deck or siding. Those jobs need more flow than this band delivers.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You wash cars and furniture. The Greenworks covers it.

maintenance.why: Debris blocks flow and strains the pump. Run clean water through the pump for a minute after soap use, then drain it fully.
Frozen water can crack the pump. Coil the hose loosely to avoid kinks.
Cold or heat accelerates fade. Keep spare O-rings and a thread-seal tape roll in the toolbox for leaky fittings.

faq.a: Not well. They lack the flow for concrete. Use them on cars, furniture and light grime. A wide tip and a safe distance protect paint and wood. Rinse soap thoroughly to avoid streaks and spotting.
They are peaks. Electric washers quote the highest value the pump reaches, not a sustained number. Check the pump label for peak and sustained values if given.

faq.q: Are cordless pressure washers worth it?
faq.a: For boats, bikes and chairs away from an outlet, yes. For real cleaning, a corded washer is stronger. Cordless washers are best treated as rinse tools.
Flow rate. Higher GPM rinses dirt away faster. Combine it with PSI to compare machines. Always compare both numbers.

faq.q: How do I store a pressure washer in winter?
faq.a: Drain the water and hose and store it indoors so the pump does not freeze and crack. Storing it dry avoids most winter problems.
